profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Collins Aerospace

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description: Skills: C++ · Rust (Programming Language) · Object-Oriented Programming (OOP)

positions.title: CS357 Numerical Methods Lead Teaching Assistant
positions.description:
Goal: Support students that are learning Numerical Methods and develop course content
•	Lead group learning assignments and assist groups that are stuck on the group assignment
•	Hold office hours and aid students in conceptual understanding and application of Numerical Methods
•	Proctor discussion forum to assist students that have questions
•	Develop and thoroughly test Numerical Methods course questions on PrairieLearn
•	Collaborate with other Teaching Assistants to review each other’s questions
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · Computer Science · Numerical Methods · HTML

positions.title: Network Systems Intern
positions.locationName: El Segundo, California, United States · Hybrid
positions.description:
- Produced extensive documentation explaining the functionality of a network traffic routing tool
- Utilized C++ to develop and test a fault-tolerance network traffic re-routing feature for a space networking tool
- Researched CORE/EMANE network emulators to facilitate development of a network emulation testbed
- Tested mobility scripting, traffic generation, and multiple network interface functionalities with CORE/EMANE
- Translated Python waveform tracking code to MATLAB and integrated into toolset
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · Matlab · Modeling and Simulation · C++ · Version Control · Programming · Software Engineer

positions.title: Flight Software and Simulation Engineer
positions.description:
Goal: Develop and launch a rocket capable of reaching the Kármán line 
•	Creating Hardware-in-the-Loop simulation to test rocket avionics and rocket control system 
•	Researched serial communication methods on Unix and Windows systems
•	Writing a cross-platform serial communication library in C++
•	Test the serial communication library testing by sending serial messages between devices
positions.insights: Skills: C++ · Computer Science · Version Control · Programming

positions.title: State Estimation & Control Chief Engineer
positions.description:
Goal: Design, build, and test rocket control systems
•	Researched efficient and viable methods of rocket drag and roll control
•	Developed extensive simulations to test theoretical performance of control systems
•	Orchestrated team meetings to evaluate control system and simulation software design
•	Constructed a Kalman Filter to optimally observe rocket states during flight
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · Control Systems Design · Numerical Simulation · Kalman filtering · Version Control

positions.title: Novel Sensors and Software Intern
positions.description:
Goal: Develop software capable of visually and numerically comparing Machine Learning (ML) labels
•	Analyzed outputs from an event-based camera to create ground-truth data that can be compared with ML labels 
•	Researched various open-source software for image annotation
•	Utilized image annotation labels in Python to create JSON files for structure and user-friendliness 
•	Created a Python library used to read and extract key data from JSON files
•	Utilized the library to create a Python program that calculates similarity between labels
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · JSON · Dictionaries · Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) · Computer Science · Version Control · Programming · Pandas (Software)

positions.title: Undergraduate Researcher
positions.description:
Goal: Develop autonomous aerobraking technology used to automate mission planning and operations
• Researched aerobraking and planet re-entry methods utilized in previous space missions
• Tested a Numerical Predictor-Corrector used to correct spacecraft trajectories on aerocapture missions
• Constructed Python scripts to facilitate data collection and simulation visualization
• Analyzed collected data to locate errors within full simulations and closed-form solutions
positions.insights: Skills: Python (Programming Language) · Data Visualization · Pandas (Software)

positions.title: NASA Student Launch Competition
positions.description:
The 2019-2020 NASA Student Launch competition required teams to design, build, and launch a rocket capable of deploying a UAV that is able to retrieve samples from within a designated area. As a member of the Illinois Space Society Student Launch Payload sub-team, my responsibilities included: 

-Researching methods of detecting and tracking a specific color with computer vision
-Developing C++ scripts to read the UAV's orientation and autonomously correct its position relative to an excavation site
-Operating ArduPilot, Gazebo Simulator and Robot Operating System to conduct UAV Software-in-the-Loop testing
-Composing and editing multiple technical reports that comprehensively described the project design process to NASA

positions.title: Micro-g NExT Challenge (2019-2020)
positions.description:
The 2019-2020 Micro-g NExT team was tasked with creating a lunar exploration tool that allows astronauts to collect samples of moon rock.

For this project, I:
-Developed highly detailed CAD models and engineering drawings with NX 12.0
-Brainstormed ideas to create a better design in terms of tool efficiency and safety
-Collaborated with the team to conceptualize possible failure modes and redesigned the tool to account for them
-Iterated through the engineering design process to ensure tool safety and efficiency

positions.title: Micro-g NExT Challenge (2018-2019)
positions.description:
The Illinois Space Society  2018 - 2019 Micro-g NExT team was tasked with designing and creating a sharp edge detection and suppression tool to be used on the International Space Station. The team also presented at the 2019 International Astronautical Congress(IAC), and won the Hans von Muldau Team Award, an international award for the best team project at IAC.  In this project, I had various assignments that included:

-Heading the search to find compatible timing belts to incorporate into the tool's main mechanisms
-Collaborating with the team to brainstorm possible tool failures and redesigning the tool to accommodate for them
-Iterating through the engineering design process to create a safe and effective tool
-Maintaining an active social media presence for the team by constantly updating it with the tool's progress
-Aiding in writing multiple documents; co-authoring a paper presented at the International Astronautical Congress

positions.title: NASA Space Grant Midwest High-Power Competition Structures Engineer
positions.description:
The Illinois Space Society Space Grant team was tasked with designing,building, and launching an efficient supersonic rocket. As a structures engineer in the project, I had to overcome many challenges to help the team reach our goal. Some accomplishments include:

-Conducting CFD with ANSYS Fluent to simulate shock waves on a transonic rocket and optimize the fin design
-Utilizing FinSim and OpenRocket simultaneously to optimize rocket fin design for transonic flight
-Researching and incorporating construction methods to create and attach fins to rocket
-Updating and organizing OpenRocket and version control for easy access and transparency

As a result, the team won 2nd place in the competition and successfully launched multiple subsonic and supersonic flights.

positions.title: MaxDrones Secretary
positions.description:
At MaxDrones, the team focused on programming a drone to perform specified tasks. In this project I have gained programming experience, and aided in numerous accomplishments:

-Utilized PS-Drone API in Python to make drone perform autonomous tasks
-Tested and debugged code to fix errors
-Gained experience with computer vision for object detection by utilizing the Haar Cascade algorithm to detect faces using the drone's camera

As secretary of the project, I helped with administrative responsibilities:

-Updated AIAA on project progress by recording meeting logs and relaying the project's progress to the technical officer
-Prepared presentations about MaxDrones that were presented at general AIAA student organization meetings

positions.title: Worldwide Youth in Science and Engineering Camp Counselor
positions.description: I became a WYSE camp counselor so that I could show prospective students the benefits of becoming a student in the Grainger College of Engineering. As a camp counselor, I was friendly and open to students, and answered their questions about the University and Engineering. I also led groups of students through night activities to show them what activities the University has to offer. In addition, I cooperated with other counselors and my supervisors to enforce the camp rules to make sure the campers were safe and felt comfortable.

honors.title: Hans von Muldau Award for Best Team Project
honors.description: The 2018 - 2019 Illinois Space Society Micro-g NExT team won this award after submitting a paper and presenting about the Micro-meteoroid Impact Detection and Suppression Tool.
honors.issuer: Issued by International Astronautical Congress · Oct 2019

honors.title: Dean's List Scholar
honors.issuer: Issued by Grainger College of Engineering · Aug 2019

volunteerExperiences.description: Through the Illinois Space Society, I have gained many opportunities to volunteer my time to expose children to Aerospace Engineering and encourage them to pursue an Aerospace or STEM-related field of study. I have volunteered during events such as Robotics Day, Franklin Academy STEAM night, and I was even on the committee that plans Illinois Space Day, in addition to a committee that is creating a Special Needs oriented Space Exploration outreach workshop. I plan on continuing to take part in educational outreach throughout my college career.
